pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 🔤 **Strand 2 — Algebra**
Using letters and symbols to describe patterns, relationships and unknown quantities.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B7.2.1)
- B7.2.1.1 — Derive the rule for a set of points of a relation, draw a table of values to graph the relation in a number plane and make predictions about subsequent elements of the relation.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- extend patterns made with objects and numbers and explain how each term differs from the one before it
- describe the rule of a relation in words such as "one more than twice"
- identify the rule in a pattern or mapping and use it to predict other terms
- locate points on the number plane, make tables of values for a rule and draw graphs
- use graphs and the number plane to solve problems

pages.title: Extending patterns
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Extend a given relation presented with and without symbolic materials and explain how each element differs from the preceding one.
Curriculum indicator B7.2.1.1.1
A **pattern** is an arrangement of objects or numbers that follows a rule. Each object or number in the pattern is called a **term**.
## ✏️ Example 5.1
Study the pattern made with matchsticks.
[[fig:m7-f19]]
Figure 5.1: A matchstick pattern made of octagons
a) Draw the 5th pattern. b) How does each pattern differ from the one before it? c) Copy and complete the table.
| **Pattern number** | **1** | **2** | **3** | **4** | **5** | **6** | **7** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of sticks | 8 | 15 |  |  |  |  |  |
**Solution**
a) Pattern 5 has 5 octagons joined in a row, each sharing one side with the next.
b) Each new octagon shares one side with the previous one, so it needs only **7 more sticks**.
c) Add 7 each time:
| **Pattern number** | **1** | **2** | **3** | **4** | **5** | **6** | **7** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of sticks | 8 | 15 | 22 | 29 | 36 | 43 | 50 |
## ✏️ Example 5.2
Study the pattern of numbers and complete the table.
| **Domain** | **1** | **2** | **3** | **4** | **5** | **6** | **7** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Co-domain | 4 | 7 | 10 |  | 16 |  |  |
a) What are the missing numbers in the co-domain? b) If the next number in the domain is 9, what is the corresponding number in the co-domain?
**Solution**
Each co-domain number is 3 more than the one before it. The rule is "multiply by 3 then add 1": 1 → 3(1) + 1 = 4, 2 → 3(2) + 1 = 7, …
a) 4 → **13**, 6 → **19**, 7 → **22**
b) 9 → 3(9) + 1 = **28**

pages.title: Keep going
pages.body: > 🔑 **Key idea: Domain and co-domain** — In a relation, the set of **inputs** is called the **domain** and the set of **outputs** is called the **co-domain** (or range).

pages.title: Describing rules in words
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Describe the rule for a given relation using mathematical language such as one more, one less, one more than twice, etc.
Curriculum indicator B7.2.1.1.2
## ✏️ Example 5.3
This table shows the cost (in GH₵) of packed breakfast for workers on a field trip.
| **Number of workers** | **1** | **2** | **3** | **4** | **5** | **6** | **?** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cost of breakfast (GH₵) | 3 | 6 | 9 | 12 | 15 | 18 | 120 |
a) Explain how the cost changes as more workers go on the trip (describe the rule). b) How many workers went on the trip if the cost was GH₵120?
**Solution**
a) The cost increases by GH₵3 for each extra worker. The rule is **"cost = 3 times the number of workers"**: n → 3n.
b) 3 × n = 120, so n = 120 ÷ 3 = **40 workers**.
## ✏️ Example 5.4
State the rule in words for each relation and complete the table.
| **Input (x)** | **1** | **2** | **3** | **4** | **5** | **Rule** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Output A | 5 | 10 | 15 | 20 |  | x → 5 times x |
| Output B | 0 | 4 | 8 | 12 |  | x → 4 times (one less than x) |
| Output C | 4 | 7 | 10 | 13 |  | x → one more than three times x |
| Output D | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 |  | x → twice (one more than x) |
| Output E | 5 | 11 | 17 |  |  | x → ? |
**Solution**
| **Output** | **x = 5** | **Rule in symbols** | **Rule in words** |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 25 | 5x | five times x |
| B | 16 | 4(x − 1) | four times one less than x |
| C | 16 | 3x + 1 | one more than three times x (thrice x) |
| D | 12 | 2(x + 1) | twice one more than x |
| E | 23 (x = 4), 29 (x = 5) | 6x − 1 | one less than six times x |

pages.title: Keep going
pages.body: > 🎯 **BECE tip** "One more than twice x" means 2x + 1, but "twice one more than x" means 2(x + 1). Read the words carefully — the order matters!

pages.title: Finding rules in patterns and mappings
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Identify the relation or rule in a pattern or mapping presented numerically or symbolically, and predict subsequent elements.
Curriculum indicator B7.2.1.1.3
## ✏️ Example 5.5
Find the rule for this pattern of tiles and predict the number of tiles in the 10th shape.
[[fig:m7-f20]]
Figure 5.2: L-shaped tile patterns
**Solution**
| **Shape number (n)** | **1** | **2** | **3** | **4** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of tiles | 3 | 5 | 7 | 9 |
Each shape has 2 more tiles than the one before. Shape 1 has 3 = 2(1) + 1 tiles. The rule is **n → 2n + 1**.
10th shape: 2(10) + 1 = **21 tiles**
## ✏️ Example 5.6
Find the rule for each mapping and the value of n.
[[fig:m7-f21]]
Figure 5.3: Two mappings
**Solution**
a) 1 → 4, 2 → 7, 3 → 10, 4 → 13: the outputs go up in 3s, and 3 × 1 + 1 = 4. Rule: **x → 3x + 1**.
b) 2 → 3, 4 → 7, 6 → 11, n → 19: outputs go up by 4 when inputs go up by 2, i.e. by 2 for each 1. Rule: **x → 2x − 1**. Then 2n − 1 = 19, so 2n = 20 and **n = 10**.
## ✏️ Example 5.7
a) The result of x in the mapping x → 2x + 3 is 3. Find x. b) The result of x in the mapping x → −2x + 5 is 45. Find x.
**Solution**
a) 2x + 3 = 3 ⟹ 2x = 0 ⟹ **x = 0**
b) −2x + 5 = 45 ⟹ −2x = 40 ⟹ **x = −20**

pages.title: The number plane, tables of values and graphs
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Locate points on the number plane, draw a table of values of a given relation, draw graphs for given relations and use them to solve problems.
Curriculum indicator B7.2.1.1.4
> 🔑 **Key idea: The number plane** — The **number plane** (Cartesian plane) is formed by a horizontal number line, the **x-axis**, and a vertical number line, the **y-axis**, which cross at the **origin** O(0, 0). Every point is located by an ordered pair **(x, y)**: first move x units along the x-axis (right if positive, left if negative), then y units parallel to the y-axis (up if positive, down if negative).
## ✏️ Example 5.8
Locate the points A(1, 2) and B(−3, 2) on the number plane.
**Solution**
[[fig:m7-f22]]
Figure 5.4: Points A(1, 2) and B(−3, 2)
A: start at O, move 1 unit right, then 2 units up. B: move 3 units left, then 2 units up. Both points are 2 units above the x-axis, so AB is parallel to the x-axis and AB = 4 units.
## ✏️ Example 5.9
Draw a table of values for each mapping on the domain {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3}. a) x → 2x + 1 b) x → x² + 2
**Solution**
a)
| **x** | **−2** | **−1** | **0** | **1** | **2** | **3** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| y = 2x + 1 | −3 | −1 | 1 | 3 | 5 | 7 |
b)
| **x** | **−2** | **−1** | **0** | **1** | **2** | **3** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| y = x² + 2 | 6 | 3 | 2 | 3 | 6 | 11 |

pages.title: Example 5.10
pages.body:
## ✏️ Example 5.10
Plot the table of values on a number plane and describe the graph.
| **x** | **0** | **1** | **2** | **3** | **4** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| y | 5 | 3 | 1 | −1 | −3 |
**Solution**
[[fig:m7-f23]]
Figure 5.5: Graph of the relation in the table
The points lie on a **straight line**. Each time x increases by 1, y decreases by 2, and when x = 0, y = 5. The rule is **y = −2x + 5** (or y = 5 − 2x). From the graph, when x = 2.5, y = 0.
## ✏️ Example 5.11
The number plane shows where animals are found in a game park. Faako is standing at the origin.
[[fig:m7-f24]]
Figure 5.6: Animals in a game park
a) If Faako walks 7 units west and 8 units south, which animal does he see? b) Which animal is closest to Faako? c) Which animal is located at (2, 7)? d) What are the coordinates of the giraffe?
**Solution**
a) 7 west and 8 south takes him to (−7, −8): the **zebra**.
b) The **monkey** at (1, −2) is closest (about 2.2 units away).
c) The **elephant** is at (2, 7).
d) The giraffe is at **(−5, 4)**.
> 💻 **ICT corner** Use a free graphing app or a spreadsheet: enter x-values in one column and a formula such as =2*A2+1 in the next. Insert an "XY scatter" chart to see the graph of the relation.

pages.title: Chapter 5 summary
pages.body:
- A pattern follows a rule; the difference between terms helps you find it.
- Inputs form the domain, outputs form the co-domain. A rule can be written in words or symbols, e.g. "one more than twice x" = 2x + 1.
- To find an input from an output, solve the equation formed by the rule.
- In the number plane, (x, y) means x across (right +, left −), then y up (+) or down (−).
- A table of values gives points to plot; points of a rule like y = mx + c lie on a straight line.
